1.q: Some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me
1.note: The elders sat before Ezekiel in order to inquire of the Lord through Ezekiel.

2.note: This is an idiom that is used to introduce something that God told his prophets or his people. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 3:16. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke this message] or [Yahweh spoke these words]

3.note: God calls Ezekiel this to emphasize that Ezekiel is only a human being. God is eternal and powerful, but humans are not. Alternate translation: [Mortal person] or [Human]

3.q: have taken their idols into their hearts
3.note: Yahweh speaks of the elders committing themselves to worshiping idols as if the elders had “taken their idols into their hearts.” Alternate translation: [have devoted themselves to idols]

3.q: have put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their own faces
3.note: Yahweh speaks of the idols that the elders worship as if they were blocks over which the elders stumble, and of being determined to worship those idols as if they had placed those stumbling blocks in front of their faces. Alternate translation: [have resolutely determined to worship the things that lead to iniquity]
This could mean: (1) the idols are a stumbling block that leads to the elders’ iniquity or (2) worshiping idols is an iniquity that causes the elders to stumble.

3.q: Should I be inquired of at all by them?
3.note: Yahweh asks this rhetorical question to emphasize that the elders should not be inquiring of him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. It can also be stated in active form. Alternate translation: [Should I permit them to inquire of me at all?] or [They should not be inquiring of me at all.] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

4.note: The word “them” refers to the “men from the elders of Israel.”

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelite people group]

4.q: who takes his idols into his heart
4.note: Yahweh speaks of the people committing themselves to worshiping idols as if they had taken their idols into their hearts. See how you translated this metaphor in Ezekiel 14:3. Alternate translation: [who devotes himself to idols]

4.q: who puts the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face
4.note: Yahweh speaks of the idols that people worship as if they were blocks over which the people stumble, and of being determined to worship those idols as if they had placed those stumbling blocks in front of their faces. See how you translated this metaphor in Ezekiel 14:3. Alternate translation: [who resolutely determines to worship the things that lead to iniquity]

4.q: I, Yahweh, will answer him according to the number of his idols
4.note: This phrase refers to the many idols that the people worship. It is implied that the severity of Yahweh’s answer will as great as the number of idols that they worship. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, will give him the answer that he deserves because he worships so many idols]

5.q: I may take back the house of Israel in their hearts
5.note: Here the word “hearts” represents the minds and affections of the people. Yahweh speaks of causing them to be devoted to him once again as if he were to capture their hearts. Alternate translation: [I will cause the people of Israel to be devoted to me again] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

5.q: their hearts that have been driven far from me through their idols
5.note: Here the word “hearts” represents the minds and affections of the people. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [who have all left me to worship their idols] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

6.note: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelite people group]

6.q: Repent and turn away from your idols! Turn back your faces from all your abominations
6.note: Both of these phrases are ways to tell the people of Israel to stop worshiping idols.
The words “repent” and “turn way” mean basically the same thing. Together they strengthen the command to stop worshiping idols.
Here the word “faces” represents the people. Alternate translation: [Turn back]

7.note: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelite people group]

7.q: who takes his idols into his heart
7.note: Yahweh speaks of the people committing themselves to worshiping idols as if they had taken their idols into their hearts. See how you translated this metaphor in Ezekiel 14:3. Alternate translation: [who devotes himself to idols]

7.q: puts the stumbling block of his iniquity before his own face
7.note: Yahweh speaks of the idols that people worship as if they were blocks over which the people stumble, and of being determined to worship those idols as if they had placed those stumbling blocks in front of their faces. See how you translated this metaphor in Ezekiel 14:3. Alternate translation: [who resolutely determines to worship the things that lead to iniquity]

8.q: I will set my face against that man
8.note: Yahweh speaks of being opposed to a person as if he were to set his face against that person. Alternate translation: [I will be against that man] or [I will oppose that man]
Here “face” is a metonym for attention or gaze, and “set my face” refers to staring. Alternate translation: [stare]

8.q: make him a sign and a proverb
8.note: Here the word “sign” refers to something that communicates a special warning to those who see it. The word proverb refers to what people will say about that sign when they see it. Alternate translation: [I will make that man to be a warning and a proverb]

8.q: I will cut him off from the midst of my people
8.note: Yahweh speaks of causing a person no longer to belong to his people as if he were cutting that person off from the people, like a person would cut a branch from a tree. Alternate translation: [I will cause him no longer to belong to my people]

When Yahweh says that people will know that he is Yahweh, he is implying that they will know that he is the one true God who has supreme authority and power. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 6:7. Alternate translation: [understand that I am Yahweh, the one true God] or [realize that I, Yahweh, have supreme power and authority]

9.q: I will reach out with my hand against him
9.note: God’s “hand” refers to what he does. Alternate translation: [I will work against him]

10.q: They will carry their own iniquity
10.note: Here the word “iniquity” represents the guilt that people incur for committing iniquity. Yahweh speaks of people suffering the consequences of their iniquity as if they were carrying the iniquity. Alternate translation: [They will suffer the consequences of their own iniquity] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

11.note: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelite people group]

11.q: will no longer wander away from following me
11.note: Yahweh speaks of the people no longer worshiping him as if they were to wander away from him and no longer follow him. Alternate translation: [will no longer stop worshiping me]

11.q: this is the Lord Yahweh’s declaration
11.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared]

13.q: when a land sins against me
13.note: Here the word “land” represents the people who live in the land. Alternate translation: [when the people who live in a land sin against me]

13.q: break the staff of its bread
13.note: Yahweh speaks of the supply of bread as if it were a staff. The word “bread” represents all kinds of food. See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 4:16. Alternate translation: [end the supply of its food] (See also: [Synecdoche](ta:figs-synecdoche))

13.q: cut off both man and beast from the land
13.note: Yahweh speaks of killing people and animals as if he were cutting them off, like a person would cut a branch from a tree. Alternate translation: [kill both man and beast in the land]

16.note: “as surely as I am alive.” Yahweh uses this expression to show that what he says next is certainly true. This is a way of making a solemn promise. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [I solemnly swear]

16.q: only their own lives would be rescued
16.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they could only rescue their own lives]

17.q: if I bring a sword against that land
17.note: The word “sword” is a metonym for soldiers who kill people using swords.
Here the word “sword” represents the soldiers of an enemy army who attack with swords. Alternate translation: [Army, go through the land]

17.q: cut off both man and beast from it
17.note: Yahweh speaks of killing people and animals as if it were cutting them off, like a person would cut a branch from a tree. Alternate translation: [kill both man and beast in the land]

18.q: only their own lives would be rescued
18.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they would only rescue their own lives]

19.note: Yahweh speaks of expressing his fury as if his fury were a liquid that he pours out from a container. Alternate translation: [I will express my fury]

19.q: cut off both man and beast
19.note: Yahweh speaks of killing people and animals as if he were cutting them off, like a person would cut a branch from a tree. Alternate translation: [kill both man and beast]

20.q: only their own lives would be rescued
20.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they would only rescue their own lives]

21.q: to cut off both man and beast from her
21.note: Yahweh speaks of killing people and animals as if it were cutting them off, like a person would cut a branch from a tree. The word “her” refers to Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [to kill both man and beast in Jerusalem]

22.note: The word “behold” here alerts us to pay attention to the information that follows.

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they will comfort you concerning the punishment]

23.note: Both of these phrases refer to what the people of Israel have done. Alternate translation: [the way they live] or [the things they do]
